institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose The Arctic University in Tromsoe (UiT) because they had courses in Marine Biotechnology. I want to specialise in algae and a semester at UiT was a good opportunity to learn more about algae and marine organisms. UiT focus on marine sciences and collect samples from the deep sea of the Arctic which I found very interesting to work with. My exchange enabled me to come into contact with colleagues and professors that can help me with my thesis on algae.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Almost all the information needed was on their website and they had a special page for exchange students or students coming from abroad. The course catalogue is also digitalized so the courses were easy to find but detailed information about the course schedules is not available. The course schedule depends on each professor and it can be quite difficult to avoid overlap in schedules. To get further information, I would recommend to mail the exchange student coordinators which usually answer quite fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The student coordinator, student housing committee, and students were all very welcoming and eager to help me upon my arrival. The student coordinator was always available and I could contact him with any minor problem I would get. The student housing committee were located close to campus, were open in office hours, and always responded mails quickly. The students were very welcoming and helpful both on- and off-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There were no housing on-campus but I lived within walking distance to campus and it was a very cozy place together with three other students. I applied through samskipnaden and I got an answer very quickly but only one month before arriving. I would recommend other students to be patient and if in doubt contact samskipnaden. I think it is quit easy to get a room but you have to be patient.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The most common transportation method is buses and they do not always arrive as frequently as in larger cities so be prepared to plan a bit a head if you want to go somewhere. Applications as mazemap, google maps and tromsoe reise are very useful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some technical problems with the registration but I just called course registration and they were able to fix it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a webpage named studentweb where you register the courses you want to take. The courses are found in the course catalogue (google course catalogue UiT and you will find it). You have to activate your mail (FEIDE and UiT mail) before you can register for course but there is a very thorough guide whih they will send to your mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guides, mail addresses of course coordinators and the web page.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted and luckily I did not have to change them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Select courses from a study like Marine Biotechnology so you don't risk that the courses are overlapping.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were equal or maybe a bit lower than the level at Copenhagen University. I felt like it was up to the individual how much work they would put into the classes and I think that was great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was very much the same as UCPH, there were both lectures, group work, and laboratory courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Marine Bioprospecting, Quantitative Microbial Biotechnology I, and Industrial Biotechnology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Marine Bioprospecting because you get to go on a real expedition and collect arctic samples. The courses focus on the arctic environment and you get to handle and process real arctic samples.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Kraft subscription for exchange students is valid until December and you have to pay an extra fee if you want to go to the gym in the last weeks of your study

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was part of Kraft which is the gym, it was really nice and they provided sauna and classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Kraft or pickleball because they are very social clubs. I would have liked to try the outdoor club but I did not have time unfortunately.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go do outdoor sports like hiking or trail running in the summer or autumn and skiing in the winter. Tromsoe is a really beautiful but there are also other places which are accessible with the bus that I also recommend to visit like sommeroeya,

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I don't think there is such a large cultural difference and it was very easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Norwegians are outdoor people so try to ask them if they want to go out hiking or ask for tips to do in Tromsoe and they will help you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They eat very early like around 5 pm but it was not really a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very happy and chill people and they like the outdoors which I appreciate.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Mail people if you have any doubts, go to a club, and go outdoors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The polar night can be quite difficult to handle and I recomment people to take vitamin D and go to UV lamp arrangements which is provided by the university.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To study Marine biotechnology and meet colleagues which have the same interests.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The polar night which can change your day rhythm

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
